title: About this portfolio
text:
This website is my learning portfolio for ISSS608 Visual Analytics and Applications. It records the methods, code, visualisations, and interpretations developed through the course’s hands-on exercises.
The portfolio is created with R and Quarto, version-controlled on GitHub, and published as a website through Vercel.

title: About this portfolio
text:
Course themes

Geospatial data import, transformation, and geoprocessing
Thematic mapping and geovisualisation
First- and second-order spatial point-pattern analysis
Spatio-temporal point-pattern analysis

The worked pages are organised under the Hands-on Exercises dropdown in the navigation bar.

title: Hands-on Exercise 1
text: This exercise introduces a reproducible geospatial workflow using sf and the tidyverse: importing spatial and aspatial data, checking geometry and attributes, managing coordinate reference systems, and performing geoprocessing.

title: Hands-on Exercise 1
text:
Learning focus

Import polygon, line, and point data with st_read().
Inspect simple-feature objects and their attributes.
assign or transform coordinate reference systems appropriately.
Convert longitude/latitude records into an sf object.
Use buffering, spatial intersection, and tidy data wrangling.

title: Hands-on Exercise 1
text:
Analysis workflow

Acquire and organise the required geospatial and aspatial datasets.
Import the datasets using paths that match this project.
Inspect their geometry types, attributes, extents, and coordinate systems.
Standardise projected data to SVY21 / Singapore TM (EPSG:3414) when distance or area is analysed.
Complete and interpret the required geoprocessing tasks.







The course website’s chap01/data/... paths belong to the lecturer’s project. Code in this repository must use the actual local data folders instead.

title: Hands-on Exercise 5
text: This exercise examines whether point events interact across a range of distances and whether the observed pattern is more clustered or dispersed than an appropriate reference process.

title: Hands-on Exercise 5
text:
Learning focus

Prepare spatial point-pattern data and a valid observation window.
Use the G-function to study nearest-event distances.
Use the F-function to study empty-space distances.
Use K- and L-functions to assess spatial dependence across distances.
Compare observed statistics with simulation envelopes.

title: Hands-on Exercise 5
text:
Analysis workflow

Import and validate the study-area and event data.
Convert the data into the structures required for point-pattern analysis.
Define a suitable null model and simulation settings.
Compute G-, F-, K-, and L-function diagnostics.
Interpret departures from the simulation envelope carefully and in context.







Conclusions depend on the observation window, edge correction, distance range, and reference process used.

title: Hands-on Exercise 4
text: This exercise studies the intensity and broad spatial distribution of point events using nearest-neighbour methods and kernel density estimation (KDE).

title: Hands-on Exercise 4
text:
Learning focus

Import, wrangle, and validate event and study-area data.
Prepare point-pattern objects for analysis.
Apply the Clark–Evans nearest-neighbour test.
Estimate spatial intensity with kernel density estimation.
Compare fixed and adaptive bandwidth approaches.
Produce a cartographically clear KDE map.
Summarise first-order patterns at planning-subzone level.

title: Hands-on Exercise 4
text:
Analysis workflow

Define the study area and clean the point-event data.
Confirm that the coordinate system is suitable for distance-based analysis.
Examine nearest-neighbour structure.
Estimate and compare density surfaces.
Interpret where event intensity is relatively high or low, with attention to boundary effects and bandwidth choice.







First-order methods describe intensity across space; they do not by themselves establish why a pattern occurs.

title: Hands-on Exercise 2
text: This exercise develops clear thematic maps from geospatial data and explores how classification, symbols, layout, and interactivity affect what a map communicates.

title: Hands-on Exercise 2
text:
Learning focus

Import and prepare the required spatial and attribute data.
Build choropleth maps with tmap.
Compare variables through small-multiple maps.
Highlight spatial features that meet a selection criterion.
Combine thematic maps with statistical charts.
Create an interactive map for exploration.

title: Hands-on Exercise 2
text:
Analysis workflow

Check the spatial data, attributes, and coordinate reference system.
Select a meaningful variable and appropriate classification method.
Design a readable static thematic map with suitable labels and legend.
Compare patterns with small multiples or a supporting chart.
Add interactivity where it improves exploration of the data.







Map design choices should be justified by the analytical question, not only by visual appearance.

title: Hands-on Exercise 6
text: This exercise extends point-pattern analysis into time, showing how the location and intensity of events evolve across temporal intervals.

title: Hands-on Exercise 6
text:
Learning focus

Prepare a study area and event data with valid spatial and temporal fields.
Visualise point events across time.
Compute spatio-temporal kernel density estimates by month and day of year.
Compare alternative approaches to temporal grouping and KDE.
Apply spatio-temporal point-pattern methods and interpret their outputs.

title: Hands-on Exercise 6
text:
Analysis workflow

Import and validate the study-area boundary.
Clean event coordinates, dates, and temporal attributes.
Explore how event counts and locations change over time.
Estimate and compare spatio-temporal density surfaces.
Interpret persistent, emerging, and changing concentrations with appropriate caveats.







Temporal aggregation can change the apparent pattern, so the selected time unit should match the analytical question.

title: ISSS608 Visual Analytics and Applications
text:
This portfolio documents my hands-on work for ISSS608 Visual Analytics and Applications. It brings together geospatial data handling, thematic mapping, spatial point-pattern analysis, and spatio-temporal analysis using R.
Use the Hands-on Exercises dropdown in the navigation bar, or select an exercise below.

title: ISSS608 Visual Analytics and Applications
text:
Hands-on exercises


Exercise 1
Geospatial Data Science with R
Import, inspect, project, wrangle, and analyse spatial data with sf and the tidyverse.


Exercise 2
Thematic Mapping and GeoVisualisation
Build static and interactive thematic maps and complement them with statistical graphics.


Exercise 4
First-order Spatial Point Patterns
Explore nearest-neighbour analysis and kernel density estimation for spatial events.


Exercise 5
Second-order Spatial Point Patterns
Study spatial interaction across distances with G-, F-, K-, and L-functions.


Exercise 6
Spatio-temporal Point Patterns
Analyse how event intensity and spatial patterns change over time.








Each exercise page follows the corresponding course chapter and provides a dedicated place for the worked analysis, interpretation, and outputs.
